title: Three-month flow history gave no clear monthly nitrate reconstruction gain at two Gulf outlets in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether flow in the previous three months improves monthly nitrate plus nitrite concentration reconstruction at two Gulf river outlets. In 624 site-months in 2000-2025, adding flow history and its current-flow interaction reduced equal-site mean squared log error by 1.65%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was -2.03% to 5.48%. Thus the test gives no clear gain. Reference fits used month effects, time, current flow and seasonal flow terms. Each reconstruction fit used the previous 20 water years. The target was a fixed USGS WRTDS-K product, not direct observations. An ordinary WRTDS check also gave no clear gain. A secondary one-year history term raised error by 3.47%. Two related outlets, revised source models, a fixed model form and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Full-record source estimation prevents an operational forecast claim. The package includes monthly inputs, code, all predictions, uncertainty draws, source hashes, an independent numerical audit and a figure.

display.caption: Annual reconstruction scores and equal-site mean squared log error reductions. Intervals resample three-year blocks and omit source-model uncertainty.
